newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-REDMAN LEADS LIONS AGAINST FREE STATE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-REDMAN LEADS LIONS AGAINST FREE STATE.

text.p: Veteran England lock Nigel Redman will captain the British Lions against Free State on Tuesday in a match which is anything but a second team outing.

The management have insisted that, in spite of the 25-16 win over the Springboks at Newlands, the fringe players can still advance their claims for the second test against South Africa in Durban on Saturday.

Redman, who only arrived as a replacement for the injured Scot Doddie Weir, will lock the scrum with fellow-Englishman Simon Shaw in a game which he describes as "the biggest challenge" of the tour to date.
"The whole tour has been a huge challenge but to go up to Bloemfontein and play at altitude -- all in a day -- makes the Free State match the biggest challenge so far," Redman said on Monday.
"Just to be selected for the Lions was beyond belief. This honour (captaining the Lions) just makes this tour get even better, although it's important that we win tomorrow's game."
Lions' manager Fran Cotton put it even more strongly.
"Free State are arguably the best team in South Africa at the moment," he said. "They are a very tough provincial team and it will be a hell of a game."
The British Lions selectors have given Redman's men every incentive to play well in Bloemfontein.
"We've told the players we're not picking the test side for Durban until Wednesday morning -- after the Free State game -- and we're continually looking for improvements," said Cotton.
Coach Ian McGeechan also stressed that selection options remained open.
"We've always said we're prepared to keep looking if the players are playing well. You get the odd injury and we're always looking tactically at what we are doing," he said.
"All those sorts of things can lead to some change of emphasis and in personnel -- and that hasn't changed.
"That's been the case in every game that we've played so far and that will be the same tomorrow."
McGeechan said that both flyhalf Gregor Townsend (bruised rib cartilage) and prop Tom Smith (dead leg) would be fully fit for selection for the Durban test within a couple of days.
The Lions' decision to take only a squad of 21 to Bloemfontein on a day trip from Durban merely echoes the pattern of the All Blacks last year.
"It's one of the facts of modern professional rugby life," said Cotton.
"With the tests on three successive Saturdays you can't afford to spend time in these places. When all is said and done, you are remembered for your test results."
The rest of the tour party will remain in Durban to continue preparations for Saturday's test at King's Park and will watch the Bloemfontein game on television.

British Lions: 15-Tim Stimpson; 14-John Bentley, 13-Allan Bateman, 12-Will Greenwood, 11-Tony Underwood; 10-Mike Catt, 9-Austin Healey; 8-Eric Miller, 7-Neil Back, 6-Rob Wainwright, 5-Simon Shaw, 4-Nigel Redman (captain), 3-David Young, 2-Barry Willias, 1-Graham Rowntree. Replacements: Nick Beal, Neil Jenkins, Kyran Bracken, Mark Regan, Jason Leonard, Tony Diprose.
